# Independent upstream CHM corpus (test-only)

These archives are **unmodified upstream bytes**, not CHMs generated by chm-kit.
`expected/` contains all 859 non-directory resources extracted by the installed
7-Zip 26.05 (`7zz t` then `7zz x`), including internal metadata/index resources.
`manifest.json` pins every archive, resource and license SHA-256, source URLs
(with source commits where known), raw Git blobs where applicable, layout observations and the independent
oracle command/version. `SHA256SUMS` also pins the manifest itself. Never replace
an oracle with chm-kit's output to make a test pass.

### Free Pascal 3.2.2 distribution / chm package 3.3.1

`fpc-3.2.2-fpdoc.chm` is the **unmodified** `help/fpdoc.chm` member of the
[official FPC 3.2.2 CHM documentation ZIP](https://downloads.freepascal.org/fpc/dist/3.2.2/docs/doc-chm.zip).
It is not a generated imitation or a GUID-patched fixture.

- ZIP: 9,301,194 bytes; SHA-256
  `cb9ebc5f333653e6c22bdbcf92ea3390f485db330d5cf9377281af0ed367ab53`.
- Retained CHM: 81,579 bytes; SHA-256
  `20d3d4932ae7cca2fa1efa033e9c4e63780788fedc96e9134c53c6f9a9d2c552`.
- `READMECHM.fpc.txt` is the unchanged `help/readmechm.txt` member. The ZIP is
  not retained; offline tests and oracle refresh need only the retained CHM.
- All **138** 7-Zip-extractable resources are retained under
  `expected/fpc-3.2.2-fpdoc/`, including `#SYSTEM`, `$FIftiMain`, index resources,
  CSS, HTML and `/_#_README_#_`. That producer resource explicitly says
  **Free Pascal's chm package 3.3.1**, despite the distribution being FPC 3.2.2.
  This is evidence from the bytes, not a claim about a known compiler invocation.
- ITSF v3, language ID 0, directory offset 120, data base 12492, VERBATIM-first,
  64 KiB window/reset interval, 15 data frames + terminal offset (16 raw
    reset-table entries) / 8 reset groups.
  Both GUID slots at offsets 24 and 40 contain
  `10fd017caa7bd0119e0c00a0c922e6ec`. The reader's header exception accepts
  exactly that pair for v3; v2 and other GUID corruptions remain rejected.

The documentation grant is **LGPL-2.0-or-later**, not LGPL-2.1-only or MIT.
`LICENSE.fpc-fpdoc.tex` preserves the entire unmodified
[`fpdoc.tex` at documentation commit 28a887047f9fa593dff284cb35b938cdb2f86268](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fpc/FPCDocumentation/28a887047f9fa593dff284cb35b938cdb2f86268/fpdoc.tex),
including Michael Van Canneyt's copyright and explicit version-2-or-later grant.
`COPYING.LIB.fpc` is the full GNU Library General Public License version 2 text
from [GNU](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/lgpl-2.0.txt).
The [complete pinned documentation source tree](https://github.com/fpc/FPCDocumentation/tree/28a887047f9fa593dff284cb35b938cdb2f86268)
and [source archive](https://github.com/fpc/FPCDocumentation/archive/28a887047f9fa593dff284cb35b938cdb2f86268.tar.gz)
are recorded as source/license evidence. **The exact binary build commit is
unknown**: the manifest deliberately leaves `sourceCommitUrl` and
`binaryBuildCommit` null. Neither the pinned documentation commit nor the producer
version establishes a reproducible build of this CHM.

**Directory compatibility is implemented:** all 147 directory entries parse.
The first PMGL at absolute 204 (4096 bytes, density 2, 145 entries) stores FPC
quickrefs for zero-based entries `4, 9, ..., 144`, rather than the standard
`5, 10, ..., 140`. First offset 46 identifies `/#TOPICS`; standard offset 61
identifies `/#URLSTR`. The final extra FPC quickref is 3888. A single exact
convention is required for each whole table; incorrect/mixed pointers reject.
FPC's overwritten FirstPMGL hint (1 instead of 0) is only repaired with verified
FPC quickrefs and the matching `0 -> 1` predecessor chain. Complete chain and
rooted-index validation remains active. See the [conformance handoff](../../conformance/README.md)
for independent libmspack/FPC source references and targeted mutation coverage.

**Terminal ResetTable compatibility is implemented:** the 168-byte table at
absolute 12869 has 16 raw entries for 15 data frames (460763 uncompressed bytes,
32768-byte frames). Its final offset 68542 equals Content length, after the last
real frame start 68150. The parser validates and consumes that exact end offset,
then exposes only the 15 real frames; the final frame has 2011 logical bytes.
The manifest separately records `frameCount: 15`, `resetTableEntryCount: 16` and
`terminalResetOffset: 68542`. Incorrect terminals/counts, duplicate or invalid
frame starts, truncation and actual Content-length mismatches remain errors.

All full-reader FPC byte/range/stream checks now pass, including the final
partial frame with no managed cache. Fresh independent `7zz t`/`x` succeeds and
matches every name, length, hash and byte of all 138 pinned resources. No fixture
bytes were patched and no expected-failure/skip marker was added. This verifies
the pinned archive, not all FPC versions or every CHM format combination.

Release CHMs are not claimed to be Git blobs or reproducible builds. The source
commits identify the corresponding releases; official download URLs and archive
hashes identify the actual binary test inputs.

The 7-Zip CHM was extracted with the already-installed trusted `7zz` from the
1,589,510-byte official installer (SHA-256
`26cb6e9f56333682122fafe79dbcdfd51e9f47cc7217dccd29ac6fc33b5598cd`).
**The installer was never executed and is not retained.** Its member `7-zip.chm`
was renamed without changing bytes; `License.txt` is retained as `LICENSE.7zip`.
No unknown executable was run. PuTTY's notice was copied unchanged from
`putty-0.83/LICENCE` in the official source tarball; its URL/hash are in the
manifest. Existing `../pychm-example/` was neither edited nor regenerated.

## Malformed archives

Eleven small samples from [libmspack commit
55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06](https://github.com/kyz/libmspack/tree/55d501976171397ccd5d5a7a1ca7da065b1d9a06/libmspack/test/test_files/chmd)
cover zero reset interval, name bounds/overread, negative span info, off-by-one,
blank/Unicode filenames and oversized 32-/64-bit ENCINTs. libmspack distributes
these under its LGPL license (`LICENSE.libmspack`); they have no separate
per-fixture license notice. Exact per-file source URLs and hashes are pinned.

`cve-2015-4467-reset-interval-zero.chm.xor` remains upstream XOR-obfuscated bytes;
the test XORs 0xFF **only in memory**, matching upstream `chmd_test.c`. Do not
open these samples in a desktop CHM viewer or execute their contents. Several
are upstream-generated ITSF v2 **malformed** structures with invalid directory
lengths. They do **not** establish working normal ITSF v2 interoperability, and
strict early rejection does not establish that later corrupt fields were reached.

## Integrity, licensing and scope

- **All content here is test-only and must stay out of npm**, especially GPL
  PyCHM data and its extracted derivatives. No blanket MIT relicensing applies.
- Raw/extracted bytes retain upstream licenses and notices, including notices
  inside the documents. Preserve `test/fixtures/** -text` and the fixture
  Prettier exclusion; do not normalize CRLF, NULs, HTML or binary resources.
- To reproduce oracle extraction **offline** with a trusted installed 7zz/7z:
  `python3 test/conformance/refresh-oracles.py` from the repository root. This
  checks pinned input/notice hashes first, uses no chm-kit module and performs no
  network downloads. It rewrites only this new fixture's expected bytes/manifest.
  Different 7-Zip versions change the tool-version/manifest hash, so review diffs.
- Valid real ITSF v2 remains missing. Other uncovered combinations include real
  GBK/UTF-16 text, LZXC v1, windows outside 64/128 KiB, and real long reset groups.
  A synthetic GBK writer differential is not a real GBK upstream corpus.
- CHMLib's main source tree contained no CHM; libmspack's tree contained malformed
  CHM tests but no normal CHM. The CHMLib Rust binding's 1.6 MB
  `topics.classic.chm` was investigated then excluded because its complete
  HelpStudio/third-party content redistribution rights could not be established.
  No large unknown-copyright assets are retained.
